notes: Taken from the paper's own ablation and stress-case tables. No projected numbers.

stress_case.title: Stress-case events
stress_case.subtitle: The two events that stretch the models furthest apart: GPT-5.5 against Kimi-K2.5.

events.name: SMCI
events.label: Financial markets - delisting crisis
events.takeaway: SMCI is built around company-specific numerical disclosures, which reward precise uncertainty handling: the GPT-Kimi gap is double-digit on both axes.

events.name: Trump Tariff
events.label: Trade policy - reciprocal-tariff escalation
events.takeaway: On the tariff event most models post their best calibration scores, yet the temporal axis opens the largest single-event gap in the whole table: 21.4 points.

question_bank_composition.title: Question-bank composition
question_bank_composition.subtitle: Drop one subset of the bank at a time and re-score. Subscripts are relative to the full bank.
question_bank_composition.takeaway: Dropping A inflates the mean the most (+7.2), so A carries most of the difficulty: models over-bet on a hot narrative continuing in the near term.

scoring_formula.title: Calibration scoring formula
scoring_formula.subtitle: The same answers re-scored under alternative rules. Gap is GPT minus Doubao.
scoring_formula.takeaway: Under every rule the GPT-Doubao gap stays positive, so the ranking does not depend on the rule; the proper scoring rules in fact widen it, which makes our weighted MAE the gentler choice.

true_false_bias.title: True/false-question bias
true_false_bias.subtitle: The calibration bank split by ground-truth polarity. Six-LLM means.
true_false_bias.takeaway: Models are much better at denying false events than at confirming true ones (76.1 against 60.3, mean bias +15.9). It is a disposition rather than raw strength: the two leaders are near balanced, Opus is the extreme at +38.0.

cutoff_gradient.title: Cutoff gradient
cutoff_gradient.subtitle: Each event's 25 prediction points split into early, middle and late terciles.
cutoff_gradient.takeaway: Later cutoffs see more of the arc and score higher (66.7 -> 67.6 -> 68.7). That is the closer-is-easier property a forecasting benchmark should show, and a basic sanity check on the construction.

dimension_mix.title: Question dimension
dimension_mix.subtitle: The same answers regrouped by what the question asks about: a concrete event, a policy move, or where opinion goes. Seven full-coverage systems.
dimension_mix.takeaway: Opinion questions are the easiest (64.4) and concrete events the hardest (58.9): models read the direction of the wind better than they call a specific event.

window_segments.title: Window segments
window_segments.subtitle: Temporal questions split by how far the event sits from the cutoff, then scored segment by segment. Segment shares: 52.4%·29.3%·18.3%.
window_segments.takeaway: The three segments differ by only 0.8 points, and the hardest is the middle one, 31-60 days (61.7): distance alone does not drive difficulty.
